the nature of conventional metaphors, their representation, and the mechanisms that allow us to learn and use them.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conventional metaphor approach to lexical semantics can account for the ability to generate and understand new uses of non-literal expressions, and the ability to understand non-literal language in context.
we are working on a theory of lexical semantics that is able to capture both conventional and novel uses of words, and that can be used for the interpretation of non-literal uses of language.

we have shown that a conventional metaphor theory can provide a principled account for a wide variety of phenomena in the domain of non-literal semantics, including the generation, interpretation, and learning of non-literal expressions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a systematic account of metaphor and non-literal language can be developed, and that such an account can be integrated with other aspects of lexical semantics and world knowledge to provide a comprehensive theory of language understanding.
the lexical semantics of a language is a complex and rich structure that includes not only literal meanings, but also a large number of conventional metaphors and other forms of figurative language.
the lexicon is not a static repository of word meaning but rather a dynamic repository for conventional metaphorical mappings and the knowledge that allows them to be used and extended.
